lines.trans: You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
Never mind the route, Mazen! What is that yellow envelope in your hand?!
Express station post, signed for at eleven-forty while you were chasing clock shadows.
Look at the sender line on the left—it is from our Room Eight mapmaker!
Open it, Nour, open it before my glasses fall right off my nose!
Arriving in Amman next Saturday for the thirtieth May anniversary at Jasmine Courtyard!
Next Saturday?! The original guest from Room Eight is coming HERE in person?!
Read the last line at the bottom—that is the part for the kitchen.

words.gram: def m sg noun with b- (at)

lines.trans: Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
Better go ask Suad about that old green garden book in Room Four right now.
Up the stairs we go—next Saturday is seven days away, and the oven awaits!

lines.trans: Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
Better go ask Suad about that old green garden book in Room Four right now.
Up the stairs we go—next Saturday is seven days away, and the oven awaits!
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Elative form of حسن (hasan), used for comparison.

examples.trans: This is better than that.

examples.text: صحتي صارت أحسن بكتير بعد ما ارتحت يومين.
examples.trans: My health got much better after I rested for two days.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian pronunciation of أحد عشر; precedes singular nouns as إحدعشر in construct.

examples.trans: We arrived at the market at eleven in the morning.

examples.text: عدينا إحدعش خطوة من البوابة للدرج.
examples.trans: We counted eleven steps from the gate to the stairs.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Used in everyday speech for a shorter route as well as a shortened word.

examples.text: رامي دايما بلاقي اختصار سريع من ورا الساحة.
examples.trans: Rami always finds a quick shortcut behind the courtyard.

examples.text: بلاش نجرب أي اختصار واحنا مستعجلين.
examples.trans: Let us not try any shortcut while we are in a hurry.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.trans: Our weekend is on Saturday.

examples.text: يوم السبت الصبح دايماً بنروح نجيب خضرة من السوق.
examples.trans: On Saturday morning we always go buy vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: You all (subject pronoun).

examples.trans: Where are you all going tonight?
Are you all ready for us to start tasting the cakes?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: A highly versatile prefix used as a preposition of place or instrument.

examples.trans: We went to work by car.

examples.text: اكتب اسمك بـ قلم الحبر على البطاقة.
examples.trans: Write your name with the fountain pen on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian form of ثمانية with interdental th > t shift.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط ساكن بغرفة رقم تمنية.
examples.trans: The mapmaker lives in Room Number Eight.
The party starts at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Standard word used in Jordanian Arabic for a part, portion, or section of something.

examples.trans: This is part of the problem.

examples.text: كل جزء من الخريطة مرسوم بدقة عجيبة.
examples.trans: Each part of the map is drawn with remarkable precision.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.text: افتح الخريطة على التلفون عشان ما نضيع.
examples.trans: Open the map on the phone so we don't get lost.
We followed the blue lines on the old map.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: I bought five books today.

examples.text: عندنا خمسة أبواب خشب بتطلع عالحديقة.
examples.trans: We have five wooden doors leading out to the garden.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Hollow Form I verb (often pronounced داق in casual Jordanian).

examples.text: مين رح يذوق التلات كيكات ويختار الأحسن؟
examples.trans: Who is going to taste the three cakes and pick the best one?

examples.text: ذقت العسل البلدي وكان طعمه روعة.
examples.trans: I tasted the local honey and its flavour was wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: He went to work in the morning.

examples.text: رامي راح عالمكتبة يدور على الكتاب القديم.
examples.trans: Rami went to the library to look for the old book.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباب.

examples.trans: Oh goodness, help us today!
Praise be to the Lord of all worlds.

meanings.note: Commonly used in blessings and exclamations like يا رحمتك يا رب.

examples.text: يا رحمتك يا رب، ضايل معنا عشر دقايق بس!
examples.trans: Have mercy, Lord, we only have ten minutes left!

examples.text: الله يرحم جدتي، كانت كلها رحمة وطيبة.
examples.trans: May God bless my grandmother; she was all mercy and kindness.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط قعد على طاولة واحد.
examples.trans: The mapmaker sat down at table one.

examples.text: هاد الرسام عمل لوحة رائعة للشارع.
examples.trans: This artist made a wonderful painting of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسأل, بيسأل).

examples.trans: Ask him what his name is on the phone!
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Primary weekday meaning is Saturday (يوم السبت); as a rural/Levantine noun can also mean a woven basket.

examples.text: سوق العسل بنفتح كل يوم سبت الصبح.
examples.trans: The honey market opens every Saturday morning.

examples.text: السبت الجاي رح نروح نجمع التوت من المزرعة.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we will go pick berries from the farm.

meanings.note: Construct cardinal numeral used directly before masculine or feminine counted plural nouns (e.g., سبع ورقات).

examples.text: مشينا سبع خطوات وبعدين لفينا شمال.
examples.trans: We walked seven steps and then turned left.

examples.text: في سبع بطاقات مخبية جوا العلبة.
examples.trans: There are seven cards hidden inside the tin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of شخصي (personal), often placed after a pronoun for emphasis (أنا شخصيا).

examples.text: أنا شخصيا بفضل كيكة العسل واللوز.
examples.trans: I personally prefer the honey and almond cake.
The manager handed us the invitation personally in the lobby.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial Jordanian noun for a broken piece, slice, or scrap of paper, bread, or stone.

examples.text: لقينا شقفة ورق صغيرة تحت الباب.
examples.trans: We found a small scrap of paper under the door.

examples.text: اقسم الكيكة وعطي كل واحد شقفة متساوية.
examples.trans: Cut the cake and give everyone an equal piece.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a month.

examples.trans: I want to travel in a month.

examples.text: بشهر الصيف بنقطف التوت من المزرعة.
examples.trans: In the summer month we pick berries from the farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: شو المكون السري اللي ضفتيه عالعجينة؟
examples.trans: What is the secret ingredient that you added to the batter?

meanings.note: Active participle of ضل ('to remain'); standard Jordanian for 'there is ... left'.

examples.trans: He has two valves left on the shelf.
How much time is left until noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: طوّل بالك ('lengthen your patience' = take it easy, hold on!) is a classic Levantine expression.

examples.text: طول بالك يا أستاذ، اقرأ الصفحة التانية!
examples.trans: Hold on, sir, read the second page!
I did not take long at the market; I came right back.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: The bedroom is very spacious.

examples.text: غرفة المكتبة هادية ومليانة كتب خرائط.
examples.trans: The library room is quiet and full of atlases.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: An alternative spelling and pronunciation variant of 'لسا', used widely in the Levant.

examples.trans: I am still studying for the exam.

examples.text: مازن لسه عم بدور عالبطاقة الأخيرة بالدرج.
examples.trans: Mazen is still searching for the final card in the drawer.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

لهون.gloss: here; hither; up to this point

meanings.en: here; hither; up to this point
meanings.note: Combines لـ (to, toward) with هون (here); used for motion toward the speaker or stopping at a limit.

examples.text: تعال لهون يا طارق عشان تشوف الرسمة.
examples.trans: Come over here, Tariq, so you can see the drawing.

examples.text: لهون وبس، خلصنا حل اللغز بنجاح!
examples.trans: Up to here and no further—we have solved the puzzle successfully!

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Colloquial active participle of مرق (to pass by); used adjectivally and verbally for someone currently passing.

examples.text: كنت مارق من جنب المخبز وشميت ريحة الكيك.
examples.trans: I was passing by the bakery and smelled the cake.

examples.text: شخص مارق بالشارع دلنا على المكتبة.
examples.trans: A passer-by in the street pointed us to the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: مديرة). Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أرسل used substantively for the sender named on a letter or parcel.

examples.text: اسم المرسل مكتوب على ظهر المغلف بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: The sender's name is written on the back of the envelope in black ink.

examples.text: وصلنا الطرد بس ما عرفنا مين المرسل.
examples.trans: We received the parcel, but we did not know who the sender was.

meanings.note: البنت المشهورة describes Layan's high-profile popularity across school.

examples.trans: Layan is well-known across the whole school.
This is a famous restaurant in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday colloquial Jordanian word for nose (more common in casual speech than أنف); plural مناخير.

examples.text: قرب منخاره من الصحن عشان يشم الهيل.
examples.trans: He brought his nose close to the plate to smell the cardamom.

examples.text: منخاري بردان من نسمة الهوا بالبلكونة.
examples.trans: My nose is cold from the breeze on the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: التقينا بالساحة الساعة تمانية ونص تماما.
examples.trans: We met in the courtyard at eight-thirty sharp.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واصلة, plural: واصلين).

examples.text: ريحة القرفة الدافية واصلة للطابق التاني!
examples.trans: The warm cinnamon scent reaches all the way to the second floor!
The bus is pulling into the station now.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.trans: The doctor gave me the medicine prescription.

examples.text: جربت وصفة الكعك تبعت خالتي وطلعت بتشهي.
examples.trans: I tried my aunt's cookie recipe and it turned out mouthwatering.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
